artworks.title: "Joris Ysegrim" and "Quastighe Jopje"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image features a portrait etching of two individuals framed within oval shapes. The left figure is an elderly man shown in a side profile, while the right figure is an elderly woman shown in a side profile. The man has distinct facial features and wears a cap, while the woman has deep wrinkles and wears a hood. The background consists of horizontal lines, and the overall tone is monochromatic.

artworks.title: "Mondighe Melis" and "Smeerighe Els"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: This image shows two portraits side by side. The portrait on the left depicts an aged man in profile with a textured cap. The portrait on the right depicts an aged woman in profile with a draped cloth on her head. Both figures are outlined with shading and set against a background of horizontal lines within oval borders. The space outside the ovals is plain.

artworks.title: "Dirck Domp" and "Zeedighe Kniertje"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image is an etching featuring two individual portraits, both captured from the shoulders up within oval frames. The person on the left is positioned with a slight three-quarter view and has prominent facial features including large eyes and a pronounced nose. They have curly hair that peeks out from under a rounded cap, and are dressed in a garment with a visible collar. To the right, another individual is shown in profile, facing the leftward figure. This person has a long nose and wrinkles that emphasize their aged facial expressions. They wear a headscarf that covers most of their hair and are also clad in a garment with a collar. The background of each portrait consists of a series of parallel lines radiating outward from the center of the frame, contributing to a sense of depth in each image. The overall tone of the artwork is monochromatic, relying on linework to define the features and clothing of each person.

artworks.title: "Rijckje Schimmel-penninghs" and "Lubbert Leever-worst"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image features two portraits, each contained within an oval frame and set against a lined background. Both portraits show head and shoulder views of elderly individuals. On the left, a person is facing forward and wears a hood or headscarf that covers their head completely. This individual's facial features are pronounced, with distinctive cheekbones and a lined texture suggesting age. Their lips are thin, and the eyes are deeply set, surrounded by wrinkles. On the right, another individual is depicted in a similar position, wearing an unusual hat with a tight fit around the head and curly hair peeking out from underneath. This person's facial features are also prominent, including sunken cheeks, thin lips, and large, attentive eyes. Both portraits are rendered in a black and white engraving style, characterized by detailed line work. The background is minimal, emphasizing the central portraits.

artworks.title: "Goelijeke Floor" and "Kinne Snavels"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image displays two portraits side by side within oval frames. The portrait on the left shows the upper body of a person facing slightly to the right. The person has distinctive facial features including prominent cheekbones and deep-set eyes. Their hair is short, dark, and appears slightly tousled beneath a cap. They are wearing a garment with a subtle texture that resembles a cloak or robe. The background within the oval frame has a lined texture. The portrait on the right depicts a similar upper body view but in profile, facing left. The subject has a pronounced nose and wrinkles, indicating age. Their head is covered with a patterned headscarf, and they are dressed in a simple garment. The background has a lined texture and both are enclosed by oval lines against a simple backdrop.

artworks.title: "Kees Geldt-sack" and "Kaarighe Truy"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image displays two upper-body portraits enclosed in separate oval frames. Both portraits depict older individuals with distinct facial features. The person on the left is facing forward, with a slight three-quarter turn of the head to the right, and has a protruding chin, a prominent nose, and a small mouth. This individual wears a rounded cap covering most of the head, with wavy hair visible at the sides. They are dressed in a garment that appears to have a collar but lacks visible detailing or embellishments. The person on the right is shown in profile, facing left, and has a similar prominent nose and chin, with a pronounced jawline. This individual wears a hood or draped fabric that partially covers the head and neck, similar to a cowl. Both portraits are set against a background of tightly spaced horizontal lines, which fill the ovals and provide a sense of texture. The overall composition is symmetrical, with the two portraits mirroring each other's placement within the elongated vertical frames.

artworks.title: "Verdorde Nel" and "Jan Afterlam"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image contains two side-by-side oval-framed portraits of older individuals. The left portrait shows an older woman with a headscarf covering most of her hair, with distinct facial features, deep lines, and wrinkles. The right portrait displays an older man with a textured cap, curly hair, and stern facial features. Both individuals are portrayed in profile, facing each other. The background features lined shading within the oval frames against a neutral textured background.

artworks.title: "Baef Schol-becx" and "Spruyt Vroegh-bedorven"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image is an engraving depicting two individuals, each shown from the shoulders up within separate oval frames. The person on the left is wearing a headscarf that drapes over their head and rests on their shoulders. Their facial features are pronounced, with a furrowed brow and deep-set eyes. The person on the right has high cheekbones, a prominent nose, and thin lips, and is wearing a soft beret-like hat. The background within the ovals is lined, providing contrast to the detailed features of the subjects, while the remainder of the background is plain and unadorned.

artworks.title: "Pater Muylaert" and "Mater Bille-bloots"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image features a two-part portrait drawing. The left portrait displays the side profile of a person with distinct angular facial features, such as a prominent nose and a defined chin, short wavy hair, and gray clothes with a draped collar. On the right is another individual in a forward-facing position with similar facial features, wearing a hood covering their head and a garment wrapping around the neck. Both portraits are enclosed in oval frames, with a background of thin parallel lines creating a textured effect.

artworks.title: "Maey Veeghde-pot" and "Pannetje Vet"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows two head-and-shoulders portraits of individuals facing forward, each enclosed within an oval frame. On the left is an older woman with pronounced facial lines, a long nose, and deep-set eyes. Her hair is mostly concealed beneath a hood that flows around her face and neck. She is wearing a cloak with visible texture over her shoulders. On the right is an older man with distinct cheekbones, a strong jawline, and a direct gaze. He has short, wavy hair partially covered by a round, textured cap. His clothing consists of a cloak that drapes over his shoulders. The background consists of parallel horizontal lines that fill the area outside the oval frames, and there is a vertical line dividing the two portraits.

artworks.title: "Erlijcke Lyn" and "Snoepighe Steeve"

Both men have distinct facial features and wear similar hooded garments. Each portrait is encased in an oval frame within the etching, set against a background of horizontal lines. The artwork is monochrome, created with etched lines for detail and depth.

artworks.title: "Beveynsde Hil" and "Listighe Jorden"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows two male portraits side by side within oval frames. The man on the left has a hood framing his face, with prominent facial features and an intense expression. The man on the right wears a cap, with curly hair seen beneath, and has a contemplative expression. Both men wear robe-like clothing. The background has lined patterns within and outside the oval frames. No jewelry or objects are visible.

artworks.title: "Foockel Frons-muyl" and "Pietje Hard-loop"

The portrait on the right shows a person with curly hair and distinct facial features. Both individuals wear collared garments. The background of each portrait consists of horizontal lines within oval frames.

artworks.title: "Aerdighe Kniertje" and "Onbekommerde Klaes"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image depicts two oval portraits side by side, showing only the upper body of two individuals. On the left, the person is in profile facing to the right. They have a prominent hooked nose and wear a head covering that drapes over and conceals their hair. On the right, the person faces forward. They have a round face and are wearing a flat, rounded cap that covers their hair, with some curls visible at the sides near the ears. Both individuals are clad in dark clothing. The background features a detailed line pattern within each oval, set against a plain surrounding area. Each portrait is enclosed in its own oval frame with minimal embellishment.

artworks.title: "Houte Klaes" and "Kommer-stoofs"

The man on the left tilts his head downward with a sideways glance, while the man on the right faces slightly towards the left. The man on the left has curly hair and prominent facial features, including a long nose and furrowed brow. The man on the right wears a hood-like garment and has less visible hair, with facial features that include a prominent nose and deep-set eyes, suggesting older age. Both portraits are enclosed within oval frames against a background of horizontal lines for texture.

artworks.title: "Ritze Stijn" and "Schurckje Sonder-Baerdt"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder

On the left, an older woman is seen in profile facing right, with her hair covered by a hood or loose fabric. On the right, an older man is depicted in profile facing left, with distinct facial features. Both are set against a lined background in an engraving style with fine details.

artworks.title: "Trijn Bulle-bacx" and "Voorsichtighe Oenne"
artworks.artist: Johannes and Lucas van Doetechum after Pieter Bruegel the Elder
artworks.description: The image shows two individuals in oval frames, each with distinct facial features and clothing. The person on the left has a long face, a prominent nose, deep-set eyes, and is wearing a hood-like head covering and a high-necked garment. The person on the right has a similar long face, a pronounced nose, deep eye lines, short wavy hair visible under a cap, and a garment covering the shoulders and neck. The background has a simple lined pattern, contrasting with the detailed engravings of the individuals. There are no visible jewelry or objects, and the style resembles a classical engraving.

artworks.title: "Hansje Singh in Veldt" and "Blaeuwe Aecht"

The left frame shows a person facing towards the viewer's right with curly hair, a prominent nose, and an open mouth. They appear to wear a textured garment. The right frame depicts an older individual with a contemplative expression, facing slightly to the left and wearing a cloth that covers their head and shoulders. Both portraits are highly detailed with fine lines, giving a classical, engraving-like appearance.

artworks.title: "Ael Pieter-mans" and "Bedorve Sloof om't Geldt"

artworks.description: The image consists of two men in bust length, set within oval frames side by side. The man on the left is depicted in a three-quarter view facing slightly to the right, with a grin and facial lines, wearing a snug cap and a garment. The man on the right is also in a three-quarter view but facing slightly left, with a somber expression, facial details, a short curly beard, and hair visible under his cap, wearing a collared garment similar to a cloak. Both figures are framed within separate decorated oval borders on a textured background.

artworks.title: "Aecht Sonder-Ziel" and "Heertje Al-te-mooy"

He has wrinkles and a somber expression, looking forward. The man on the right has curly, short hair and wears a flat cap. He has age lines and looks slightly upward with a thoughtful expression. The background of each portrait is lined, and the image is rendered in a monochromatic, etching-like style.

artworks.title: "Oprechte Lammert" and "Deughdighe Geertruyd"

artworks.description: The illustration features two busts within oval frames, showing the head and shoulders of both individuals. On the left, a person in three-quarter view faces right, wearing a cap and a robe. The individual has short, curly hair under the cap and defined facial features, including prominent eyebrows. On the right, a person in profile faces left, wearing a head cover similar to a hood and a high-collared garment. The profile highlights the nose, lips, and chin. Both figures wear shaded, textured clothing, indicative of historical attire. The background consists of fine, horizontal lines outside the oval frames, giving the image a classic appearance.

artworks.title: "Keesje Licht-hart" and "Verblinde Swaen"
